summary: Pend Oreille County, WA summit lookout: L-4 cab built 1930, gone after 1958 (sources differ on removal vs fire); only a firefinder pedestal and few beams remain.

facts.design: L-4 cab, built 1930, on the summit near Ione
facts.status_note: Cab removed, destroyed or burned in 1958 (sources differ); Willhite finds no visible footings in 2026 but a firefinder pedestal; SummitPost reports a few beams and a rusted Osborne Firefinder platform

access.note: Summit is within Colville National Forest and reached by a hike; the trailhead is at a gated road. SummitPost says the lower west and southern flanks are probably private timber land.

visit.trail_note: Willhite: Ione Bridge, Sullivan Lake Road 4.4 miles to Dry Canyon Road, FR1936; trailhead at a gated road 7.3 miles from Sullivan Lake Road; wire in the boulder field on the route to the summit.

events.note: L-4 cab built on the summit
Register says the L-4 cab was removed in 1958
firelookout.com says the L-4 cab was destroyed in 1958
Willhite says the cab was burned in 1958; his page refers to a picture of the cab burning
Registered December 17, 2012, nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed; Willhite says burned and refers to a picture of the cab burning. The story reports that the sources differ.
The Register gives 6,784 ft (2,068 m); Willhite gives 6,790 feet. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Fate is disputed: removed (Register), destroyed (firelookout.com), burned (Willhite, with a photo caption of the cab burning). A search summary said no source describes the cab burning; the fetched Willhite page does say 'In 1958, the cab was burned', so the story uses it. The 2026 visit is Willhite's, not ours. An AllTrails search snippet (about 5.5 miles out and back) was not fetched and is not used. No Forest Service record found. The brief's kind 'ground' is not contradicted, but Willhite says the cab had a wood foundation.
